signal: Nextech launched Cora Scribe AI clinical notes and partnered with Ocuco; named Best in KLAS for Ambulatory Specialty EHR

email.body1:
Cynthia, saw Nextech launched Cora Scribe and earned Best in KLAS for ambulatory specialty EHR.

Momentum like that opens more specialty practices as prospects than the team can personally cover before they cool off. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Nextech off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Cynthia, quick follow-up for Nextech.

A new AI product usually expands the in-market list faster than headcount can keep up, and the coverage gap shows up late as a missed quarter. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the number.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Nextech needs to hit target this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Cynthia, last bit of proof for Nextech.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Nextech's reply rate likely compares to other healthcare-SaaS vendors. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Cynthia, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Launching Cora Scribe is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a healthcare-SaaS motion? I'll tailor it to Nextech either way.
